definitions.explanation: The quality or degree of hot weather. Derived from the adjective {暑|あつ}い (hot weather). Refers specifically to atmospheric heat, not the temperature of objects.

examples.japanese: {今年|ことし}の{暑|あつ}さは{異常|いじょう}だ。
{暑|あつ}さに{慣|な}れるまで{時間|じかん}がかかった。
examples.english: It took time to get used to the heat.

examples.japanese: {連日|れんじつ}の{暑|あつ}さで{体調|たいちょう}を{崩|くず}す{人|ひと}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: The number of people falling ill due to the consecutive days of heat is increasing.

notes:
USAGE:
Derived from {暑|あつ}い (hot weather) + さ (nominalizer). Refers exclusively to atmospheric/weather heat. For the heat of objects or liquids, use {熱|あつ}さ (from {熱|あつ}い). For thickness, use {厚|あつ}さ (from {厚|あつ}い).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {暑|あつ}さに{負|ま}ける: to be beaten by the heat
- {暑|あつ}さ{対策|たいさく}: measures against the heat
- {真夏|まなつ}の{暑|あつ}さ: midsummer heat
- {暑|あつ}さが{和|やわ}らぐ: the heat eases

HOMOPHONE NOTE:
- {暑|あつ}さ: heat of weather (this entry)
- {厚|あつ}さ: thickness
- {熱|あつ}さ: heat of an object (hot to the touch)
